On October 16, 2026, Union Pacific Corporation (the Company) announced that Jennifer L. Hamann plans to retire as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer effective in early 2027. Until Ms. Hamann's retirement, she will continue to maintain her current responsibilities in her role as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer. The Company will announce additional details about this transition in the future. Item 7.01 Regulation FD Disclosure. The Company issued a press release regarding the retirement of Ms. Hamann as Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer effective in early 2027, which is furnished as Exhibit 99.1. Item 5.02 Departure of Directors or Certain Officers; Election of Directors; Appointment of Certain Officers; Compensatory Arrangements of Certain Officers. On October 15, 2026, Erasca, Inc. (the Company) decided to realign its leadership responsibilities to support the development and potential commercialization of its RAS-targeting programs. Responsibilities currently overseen by the Chief Operating Officer are transitioning to other members of the Company’s leadership team in order to streamline the Company’s reporting structure. Accordingly, the employment of Nicholas (Nik) Chetwyn, Ph.D., the Company’s Chief Operating Officer, will terminate effective November 2, 2026. Item 5.02 Departure of Directors or Certain Officers; Election of Directors; Appointment of Certain Officers; Compensatory Arrangements of Certain Officers. On October 13, 2026, the Board of Directors (the “Board”) of AutoNation, Inc. (the “Company”) increased the size of the Board to ten directors and appointed Mark Stewart as a member of the Board, effective immediately. The Board determined that Mr. Stewart qualifies as independent under the director independence standards set forth in the Company’s Corporate Governance Guidelines and the applicable listing standards of the New York Stock Exchange. Mr. Stewart will participate in the Company’s non-employee director compensation program, pursuant to which he will receive an annual Board retainer of $50,000 for service on the Board. For 2026, the Board retainer will be prorated based on time served during the year. Mr. Stewart will also be entitled to receive expense reimbursement in connection with meeting attendance. As a non-employee director, he will be eligible to receive equity awards in the future under the AutoNation, Inc. 2024 Non-Employee Director Equity Plan. Item 7.01 Regulation FD Disclosure. On October 16, 2026, the Company issued a press release announcing Mr. Stewart’s appointment as a member of the Board. A copy of the press release is furnished as Exhibit 99.1 to this Current Report on Form 8-K. The information furnished pursuant to this Item 7.01, including Exhibit 99.1, shall not be deemed “filed” for purposes of Section 18 of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the “Exchange Act”), or otherwise subject to the liabilities under that Section and shall not be deemed to be incorporated by reference into any filing of the Company under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, or the Exchange Act, except as shall be expressly set forth by specific reference in such filing.
